requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O1 (must pass: yes)
requirements.statement: With `Blocking: must-pass only` in verification.md and at least one must-pass criterion, a run whose open failures are all on non-must-pass criteria ends `satisfied`; the result, state file and report list those failures, and each is written to discovered.jsonl as a product follow-up row (rankClass product, blocksFeature false).

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O2 (must pass: yes)
requirements.statement: With no blocking setting (section absent, line absent, or verification.md missing or unreadable), with `Blocking: all criteria`, or with no must-pass criterion marked, a failure on any criterion still prevents `satisfied`; /verify-build fix rounds never build a failure the run listed as non-blocking.

requirements.source: TRD Objectives table, row O3 (must pass: yes)
requirements.statement: A failure on a must-pass criterion prevents `satisfied` under either setting, including when the Judge's exit wrongly says `satisfied`; applyMustPassRecheck and custody behave as today for must-pass criteria.
An invalid Blocking value (anything other than `all criteria` or `must-pass only`, or two Blocking lines) is refused: verification is not run and the stop reason names the offending line.
The Judge never judges materiality and never applies the blocking policy; the policy is applied only by the workflow script, from the must-pass marks and the owner's setting.

The four-part definition from issue #113 (main user flow broken; data lost or corrupted; private data exposed; money or AI spend charged wrongly) is stated in TRD and success-definition authoring guidance as the test for must-pass marks, noting that verification-check rows never carry a must-pass mark and so never block under must-pass only.
/verification-setup asks for the blocking policy, offering `all criteria` as the default, and writes it in a form the parser reads.

The shipped verification.md template carries the new short section with `Blocking: all criteria`, and a project still holding the current unfilled template is still recognised as unfilled after the template changes.

A headless fixture run with the policy set to must-pass only, one must-pass and one non-must-pass seeded defect, shows the non-must-pass failure listed as non-blocking, filed as a follow-up, and the outcome satisfied only once the must-pass defect is met.

tasks.description: Add `## 5c. Blocking policy` to the shipped verification.md template with the Blocking line (default all criteria); add readBlockingPolicy beside readCoverageFloor and its read-blocking-policy CLI subcommand; freeze the current template as a fixture and add its digest to KNOWN_UNFILLED_DIGESTS.

decideNext gains an optional blocking input; under must-pass with a non-empty mustPass, a base exit-stalled or exit-stuck whose open gaps are all non-must-pass (and no unbuilt) becomes exit-satisfied with a nonBlocking key added only when the conversion fires.

Add recordNonBlockingFollowups and the record-nonblocking CLI that writes deduplicated product follow-up rows to discovered.jsonl; renderReport prints a Not blocking line only when nonBlocking is non-empty.

Workflow verify-functional.js validates args.blocking, adds applyBlockingPolicy called inside runRegressionPass before its syncState (demotes unsafe satisfied exits, converts non-must-pass-only stalls/stucks under must-pass), makes mustPassCheckState ignore non-must-pass not_met under must-pass, and returns nonBlocking on every result path; updates docs/TRD/functional-verification.md section 3.3.

implement-trd.md and verify-build.md read the blocking policy via read-blocking-policy, pass it as the 31st args field, stop on invalid, carry nonBlocking into readouts and run record-nonblocking, and skip non-blocking ids in verify-build fix rounds; update field-count assertions in the two command test files.
Custody regression guard test only: a non-must-pass not_met criterion in a satisfied state does not appear in reconcile reverify or affectedIds. No change to custody.js.

Additive authoring guidance: the four-part must-pass test in trd-authoring.md, plan.md Objectives templates, create-trd.md and the functional-verification contract, stating no stage applies it to a failure and that check rows never block under must-pass only.
verification-setup SKILL.md gains a Blocking policy topic and section (all criteria offered first, both written forms, read-blocking-policy re-check after writing), with test assertions.
Mirror every changed packages/core lib, workflows, commands and contracts file, and the verification-setup skill, into the vendored .claude/ copies; full Jest battery must pass.

[LIVE] Headless fixture scenario test/smoke/scenarios/verify-blocking-policy.sh in the fixtures environment, with one must-pass and one non-must-pass seeded defect under must-pass only; register it in run-smoke.sh and the smoke README.

[defect, amendment] read-blocking-policy throws EISDIR or a permission error on an existing but unreadable verification.md instead of returning the all-criteria default (O2); fix every instance of this weakness in the feature's touched files and add a test.
[test-gap, amendment] The FIX-010 fixture scenario has never been run live, so there is no evidence for O9; run it and fix every instance of the same gap across touched files.

could_not_verify: Validation against product requirements was not checked: the TRD has no PRD, its source is the PM's instruction of 2026-11-12 (issue #113), which was not supplied to the audit, so whether the TRD omits or distorts that instruction is unchecked.
Promises stated only in prose were not traced: a checkable promise stated only in Intended Change, Decision or Non-Goals was not traced to code or tests.

FIX-010 (the live fixture scenario) can come back inconclusive: it relies on a live Debug leaving the non-must-pass defect open, and a Debug that fixes it gives INCONCLUSIVE, not proof. The scenario has not been run.

The coverage-floor recommendation may drift lower under must-pass only: recommendCoverageFloor (packages/core/lib/functional-verification.js ~:1196) learns from satisfied runs, so converted runs with not_met criteria can lower the recommended floor. Reported, not changed.
open_questions: OQ-1: Should a non-must-pass unbuilt criterion also stop blocking under must-pass only? Assumed no (unbuilt still blocks); recorded as an OWNER-CALL in the TRD Decision section. Owner-only: no.
